architecture.mechanism: Generator-side inverter control that modulates electromagnetic torque to reduce the instantaneous torque mismatch with mechanical input torque, thereby damping drivetrain torsional vibrations.
architecture.intervention: Add a torque-damping controller to the vehicle's electric drive (or hybrid powertrain) inverter that actively adjusts electromagnetic torque to counteract measured rotational speed oscillations at the output shaft, using a resonant integrator tuned to the dominant shake/wobble frequency.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced torsional oscillation amplitude at the drivetrain output shaft, eliminating the felt vehicle shaking and wobbling across various speeds without warning lights.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument the drivetrain with a torque/speed sensor at the output shaft, command the controller to engage over a 0–120 km/h sweep, and measure whether the peak-to-peak shaft speed ripple decreases by at least 50% versus the un-controlled baseline; repeat on a shaker/road-test and compare driver-rated shake severity before vs. after enabling the controller.
